record.paper_title: Open Problems in Understanding the Nuclear Chirality
record.original_question: How can the particle-rotor model for nuclear chirality be extended beyond a rigid triaxially deformed core so that the quadrupole deformation parameters β and γ and the particle-hole configuration are not fixed inputs, but instead change self-consistently with nuclear rotation and feed back on whether chiral doublet bands appear?

evidence.quote: Although the particle rotor model has been applied to investigate the nuclear chirality extensively, it is a phenomenological model based on a rigid triaxially deformed core.
Therefore, the response of the deformation and triaxiality with the nuclear rotation as well as their influence on chirality are beyond the current version of PRM.
Naturally, one must go beyond the limit of rigid γ deformation in the future study of the nuclear chirality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the standard particle-rotor model (PRM) used to describe candidate chiral doublet bands in atomic nuclei, the nucleus is modeled as one or more valence nucleons (particles and/or holes in specified single-particle orbitals) coupled to a rigid triaxially deformed rotor whose quadrupole deformation parameters β and γ, together with the particle-hole configuration, are fixed external inputs. Chiral doublet bands arise when the total angular momentum vector lies out of any principal plane of the triaxial shape, producing two near-degenerate ΔI = 1 bands of the same parity.

Construct an extension of the PRM, formulated in the laboratory or intrinsic frame with a Hamiltonian of the form

  H = H_core(β, γ; Î) + H_sp(β, γ; configuration) + H_coupling,

in which:
1. The deformation parameters β and γ are dynamical collective variables (rather than fixed numbers), governed by a collective Bohr-type kinetic energy and a potential V(β, γ; I) that depends on the angular momentum I.
2. The particle-hole configuration occupying the valence orbitals is not prescribed a priori but is determined self-consistently together with (β, γ) at each spin I, e.g. through a variational or constrained mean-field procedure coupled to the rotor degrees of freedom.
3. The coupled equations of motion produce a feedback loop in which nuclear rotation modifies (β, γ) and the occupied configuration, and these in turn modify the moments of inertia, the single-particle alignments, and hence the conditions for the appearance, stability, and disappearance of chiral doublet bands.

Specify such a model precisely (Hamiltonian, collective metric, quantization, boundary conditions in (β, γ)-space, treatment of the valence configuration, and observables for E2/M1 transitions and energy staggering), and determine the criteria — in terms of the spin-dependent equilibrium values β(I), γ(I) and the self-consistently selected configuration — under which chiral doublet bands emerge and persist as functions of I.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that going beyond the rigid triaxial PRM for nuclear chirality remains an active research direction. Various extensions have been proposed (reflection-asymmetric triaxial PRM, TAC + RPA, collective Hamiltonian methods, IBFFM, generalized coherent state, projected shell model, self-consistent cranking studies), and self-consistent treatments have so far suggested that aplanar chiral configurations are often unstable. However, a fully dynamical PRM in which β, γ and the particle-hole configuration evolve self-consistently with rotation and feed back on chirality has not been established as solved; the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Specific features and symmetries for magnetic and chiral bands in nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Nuclear chirality has been investigated with many approaches, including the triaxial particle rotor model, the tilted axis cranking model, the TAC + RPA, the collective Hamiltonian, IBFFM, the generalized coherent state model and the projected shell model.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple frameworks beyond rigid PRM are under active development, indicating no single accepted self-consistent extension.

status_evidence.title: Interpretation of chiral symmetry breaking and octupole correlations by the reflection-asymmetric triaxial particle rotor model
status_evidence.snippet: Reflection-asymmetric triaxial particle rotor model extends PRM to include octupole correlations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions still treat deformation parameters as fixed inputs, not self-consistently coupled to rotation.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic quantum ideal triaxial rotor model and related self-consistent cranking model
status_evidence.snippet: Self-consistent cranking studies find aplanar chiral configurations to be unstable when triaxial deformation is treated self-consistently.
status_evidence.claim: Self-consistent treatments give partial but inconclusive results regarding chirality, leaving the unified PRM extension open.
